institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard that Trondheim was a great student city with a cool atmosphere for young people, I had visited the city once before and thought the University was nice, the city cosy including the opportunity to learn how to ski during my exchange. Very nice courses in psychology as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *

questions.answer: It was the best half year of my life.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the busses around the city are easy to figure out, so it's not a problem at all not to live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Voll studentby wasn't cosy. Many of my friends lived there and had a very different experience than me with my housing. I had a much better stay because the atmosphere of my off campus housing was much more homely.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. They had a nice course catalog from where I could see all courses available in English and for exchange students. I changed courses many times, which was easy. I wrote to some of the lecturers to get information about the different courses, whom responded back quickly. Registration for exam was in the same platform and very easy as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NTNU's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I ended up having very exiting courses, and got the courses I wanted even though it had a limited access.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register all the courses you are considering and go to the first 1-2 lecturers. Decide after that which courses you want to keep and delete. In that way you don't miss any classes and get to consider all of them, since it can be difficult to know in advance which courses that are actually what you think, it is.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were fine, pretty much the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Personality Psychology, Social Psychology, Introduction to Norwegian History and "Psykiske lidelser".

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both Personality Psychology, Social Psychology, Introduction to Norwegian History and "Psykiske lidelser". They were very very interesting and the history course was easy which left you with more time to enjoy your stay, do social activities etc.

questions.answer: SIT fitness center. Very nice with a lot of fitness classes for other student you could easily meet there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SIT fitness center

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: HAVET arene to bath in the ocean and go to sauna, Våttakammen in Bymarka (the nature area where you can camp, walk and run, and see and elg if you are lucky). Samfundet! A huge place for student hosting parties, bingo night etc. Cava sunday at Bermuda club om Solsiden. Here they drink cava and party on Sundays from the morning.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I come from Denmark so it's pretty much the same.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be voulenteer at Samfundet

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are so active. So many oppurtunties. Very kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have a great savings! Go to Samfundet! Go outside Trondheim city as well, there are so many beautiful places nearby even though it doesn't seem like it (for instance go on a koie tour, in that way you really experience Norwegian nature).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hmm I can't think of any right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I meet from my home university and my norwegian roommates - and all the experiences we got together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out everything about course registration, Erasmus, etc alone. Not missing a deadline etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
